column8: Tue 17 Nov: store only; read Constantinides at source before citing (UNVERIFIED, four secondary accounts); his result favours policies that use later information, which l.17 rules out, so cite it only against a fixed 2030 schedule, never for the one-day move.

Tue 17 Nov: 3c store and References: Rozeff's lump-sum premium (abstract read at source) is the textbook result the one-day move mirrors; cite the 40 of 65 years with his equal-risk caveat, never as Laura's odds.
Tue 17 Nov: 3c, why the half moves at once: Rozeff's own remedy for a steadier result is a smaller fraction moved at once, not a staggered sale; explains IPS l.15's choice and changes nothing.
Tue 17 Nov: store only: the mechanism under rows 3 and 5 (a ramp loads the result on the months it is most invested); Hayley read at source, Rozeff's wording secondary.
Tue 17 Nov: store only: verified at source that a constant mix beats a ramp at almost the same mean; never cite its 50:50 as support for Laura's half kept, as the row says.
Tue 17 Nov: store only: averaging helped only for single stocks, and VT holds 10,185 stocks (Q1c-037), so the index result applies; certainty equivalents are hard to say plainly.

Tue 17 Nov: 3c store: Vanguard's two-thirds, read in a re-hosted copy (cite Vanguard, not the host); drop the 54.6% and 63.3%, the card's stylised model and not in NUMBERS, unless the numbers owner registers them.
Tue 17 Nov: store only: Vanguard's loss count is fine; at most one $5,000 step is the card's stylised house model, not NUMBERS (its history has two steps in 0.1%), so drop it or register it first.
Tue 17 Nov: store only: the newest Vanguard test, read at source; useful only to say why people ask for averaging (loss aversion); one-year horizon, three-month splits, cash at 0%.

Tue 17 Nov: store, the logic behind 3c's judge's note: Statman shows selling in parts keeps risk on longer when choosing today; under l.15's deadline the parts start earlier, so never cite it as saying one day keeps risk longer.

Tue 17 Nov: 3b, her flexibility: Statman's regret cure for a sale is to sell only part, which the half kept already does after the move (IPS l.15); say it does this too, never that it was built for it.
Tue 17 Nov: store only: Statman 1995 (abstract) explains why someone may ask to sell bit by bit, a normal preference with a known cost; the anchor for row 13.
Tue 17 Nov: twin of row 12: Dichtl and Drobetz only confirm Statman's normal-not-rational reading (abstract); keep one cite.
Tue 17 Nov: presentation guard for 3c: never argue the move date from an average price; the only test is the stated top; Hayley read at source, stylised tree.
Tue 17 Nov: store only: Cho and Kuvvet verified (averaging trades return for risk); the $400 of mean top and 13% less spread are the card's stylised model, not NUMBERS, so drop them or register them.
Tue 17 Nov: twin of row 5 (a constant mix beats averaging), read only in Hayley's summary; row 5 is verified at source.
Tue 17 Nov: store, 3c defence: averaging out wins only if 2030 prices are mispriced in a way Laura could know; the IPS takes no market view (l.17), so no case; one model, read in part.
Tue 17 Nov: store only: a retiree drawdown rule; the IPS sets no spending rule for the half kept after 2033, so never offered as a plan step, and never for the ten (IPS l.11).
Tue 17 Nov: twin of rows 5 and 15 (averaging's lower Sharpe ratio); authors only secondary; cite row 5.
Tue 17 Nov: the 2008 target-date losses are in the store as Q3a-020 (SEC 2010, which says cite one source); this row's reading (the damage came from shares held at the date) is Q3a-020's own use.

Tue 17 Nov: store only: the labels to and through are not in the testimony, so cite the description, not the labels; never call the moved half a glide path (H7-057, Q39-011: one dated trade, nothing glides).
Tue 17 Nov: twin of Q39-011 (Estrada's glidepath critique, read in abstract and the author's copy, with the reply already recorded); this row rests on IESE's summary only.

Tue 17 Nov: store only: the square root of 7/9 check is sound for the shares' part of the top in the card's stylised model (floor and yields fixed); never as the spread of the register's top, which also moves with the floor and yields.

Tue 17 Nov: 3c, answers store H8-065's open question (why not an average?): one day on 1 Jan 2031 states a slightly higher top on average; every figure is the stylised model (floor fixed, scripts not in the repo, 1-in-20 low $110,000 against NUMBERS' $95,000), so words only until the numbers owner registers it.
Tue 17 Nov: 3c, the regret in Laura's unit (about one future in ten, one $5,000 step); stylised, not NUMBERS; never confuse its 12.0% with 8r's 12.0% for a 1 April move.
Tue 17 Nov: store, Q&A only: never VT bought in 1926, 1933, 1934 or 2006 (VT launched June 2008, Q1c-037): say US stocks bought then; the figures are the stylised model, not NUMBERS.
Tue 17 Nov: store only: confirms row 3 on the stylised model (under $100 of spread); not in NUMBERS, and a part moved in 2030 is no plan step: NUMBERS 8r keeps one move on 1 Jan 2031.
Tue 17 Nov: store, 3c: averaging into 2031 is what l.15 rules out, 8r's later-date bet spread over twelve dates; a reason the plan does not, never a change; $401 and $7,024 are stylised, not NUMBERS.

Tue 17 Nov: 3c and Table 3 row 5: l.15 sets when, not how; one day is the register's choice inside it (8r: 1 January is before every possible first meeting, and the range rule is written for one move day); never not yet owned for longer.
Tue 17 Nov: store, 3e defence: level triggers are mainstream for US pensions (CEM 2018, read in part), so a judge may ask why Laura has none; pair with Q7-025 and row 31.

Tue 17 Nov: 3e or Table 3 note, why no trigger: Aon's back-test says triggers never lift the worst periods, the end co-sponsors need held; a reason the plan does not, never a change (l.15 a date, l.17 two reasons); read in excerpts.

Tue 17 Nov: 3e, Aon's pattern on Laura's plan as a reason the plan has no trigger, never a change; stylised and not NUMBERS (its 38.0% at least $120,000 against the register's 46.0%), so the numbers owner reruns it on the register before any figure.
Tue 17 Nov: store only: weak counter-evidence (one student thesis, a calm five years); too weak for the reference list.
Tue 17 Nov: store, a cross-field echo for 3c or 3e: averaging a sale trims both tails; Laura's discipline is already a date (l.15); extension bulletin read in part.
Tue 17 Nov: store, the sharpest disanalogy: averaging suits a seller with a yearly flow; Laura states one figure once, so there is no average to match.
Tue 17 Nov: store, the farm version of l.15's date and l.17's no market reason: a sale date fixed in advance and kept; two sources read in part, a different market.

Tue 17 Nov: Table 3 row 5 note or 3e: institutions sell in tranches because of size (Lloyds, 15% of volume); Laura's $18,495 (8r) against VT's 0.01% spread (NUMBERS 4) has no such reason; VT's daily volume not looked up, so cite the spread only.
Tue 17 Nov: twin of row 37 (a seller too large for one day uses a trading plan); keep Lloyds as the one example.
Tue 17 Nov: Norway's 2007-09 phase-in is in the store as Q7-027 with stronger sources; this row's reading (a long transition happened to help) is luck, and a purchase, so it adds nothing for a sale.

Tue 17 Nov: 3c conceit: two inkings, two dates may describe the one-day move, never be its reason (a conceit turn is never the evidence; the reason is 8r and the range rule written for one day); never in tables or co-sponsor words.

Tue 17 Nov: 3e restates Table 3: share prices are watched at any level (row 6, Watch), never with a level that sets off a trade; drop the claim that every source agrees (rows 17 and 33 do not); the evidence is Aon and the card's model.
Tue 17 Nov: store only: a secondhand Samuelson quote about trustees averaging in; read Samuelson (1994) at source before any use, and it is too strong for stakes of one $5,000 step.
